# Protocols

<!-- Generated by `npm run train` from the sources each rule cites. To change a rule for good, change its source or say so in training/feedback.md; the next training run regenerates this file. -->

- **Spend a single-use item (authorization code, device code, auth_req_id, PAR request_uri, initial access token, paused-flow state, a refresh token being rotated) atomically through its row's concurrency token. Treat the loser of a race as a second spend or reuse and answer with the protocol error for a used item (for example `invalid_grant`, 400), never a 500. Never retry a spend-once operation after it loses a race.** A concurrent second spend has to get the same answer as a sequential one. A spend requires the grant to be active, so retrying after a lost race would spend it twice. *Check:* In code that consumes, revokes-once or replaces-once a single-use item, check that the store's concurrency exception around update and save is caught and mapped to the 'not found / already used' result, that no caller lets it escape as a 500, and that the save is not wrapped in a concurrency retry. <sub>Identity ADR-1012; Identity ADR-1222</sub>
- **Make every grant revocation go through the one grant service, and when its save loses a concurrency race, read again and retry. Don't report success without revoking, and don't fail on the first lost race.** A revocation is correct whatever state its caller read. Failing answers 500 where RFC 7009 §2.2 requires 200 and leaves the token active; reporting success without revoking leaves grants active after logout. *Check:* Look for revocation code that stamps revocation times directly through a store, catches the concurrency exception and returns success, or doesn't retry. <sub>Identity ADR-1222</sub>
- **Implement grant revocation as an idempotent soft revoke that stamps a revoked timestamp and keeps the row: revoking an already-revoked grant changes nothing and still returns 204, and every runtime lookup treats a revoked grant as inactive.** Revocation must leave an audit trail, and a soft revoke is what makes DELETE idempotent and safe to retry. *Check:* Flag hard deletes of grant rows, an error or non-204 for an already-revoked grant, and runtime lookups that ignore the revoked timestamp when deciding whether a grant is active. <sub>Identity ADR-1020</sub>
- **Require PKCE with `S256` on every authorization-code flow: a client sends a `code_challenge` with S256 and freshly random `state` and `nonce`, and an authorization-code token request always carries `code_verifier`. A client that finds a provider advertising `code_challenge_methods_supported` without `S256` fails with a provider exception; a missing list is accepted.** PKCE binds the code to its initiator and fresh state and nonce defend against CSRF and replay. A missing list does not mean S256 is unsupported. *Check:* Look for a missing `code_challenge`, the `plain` method, reused or non-random state/nonce, an optional `code_verifier` on authorization-code requests, or discovery handling that rejects a missing list or ignores a list without S256. <sub>Identity ADR-1285; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity ADR-1275</sub>
- **On the server, treat a `code_challenge` without a `code_challenge_method` as having no method, never a defaulted one. Refuse methods the operator hasn't listed at the authorization endpoint and methods with no registered transformation at the token endpoint. Answer a missing or malformed code_challenge with `invalid_request` (authorization and PAR endpoints) and a missing, malformed or mismatched code_verifier, a verifier sent for a code with no challenge (PKCE downgrade), or an unregistered method with `invalid_grant`.** OAuth 2.1 makes the method required and defaulting would revive RFC 7636's `plain`. RFC 7636 §4.4.1, §4.6 and RFC 9700 §4.8.2 map these failures; accepting a verifier for an unbound code lets a downgrade through. *Check:* Look for a missing method defaulted to `plain` or `S256`, acceptance of any registered method without the configured list, wrong error codes on PKCE failure paths, or a token handler that ignores a code_verifier when the code was not bound. <sub>Identity ADR-1144</sub>
- **In an OAuth client's authorization callback, validate the RFC 9207 `iss` response parameter against the issuer pinned in the stored login transaction before exchanging the code; when the provider advertises `authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported`, require it.** Checking `iss` first stops a mix-up attack from sending the code to the wrong provider's token endpoint. *Check:* Look for callback handlers that call the token endpoint before comparing `iss`, never check it, or take the expected issuer from the response instead of the stored transaction. <sub>Identity ADR-1290; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md</sub>
- **Carry `redirect_uri` and `post_logout_redirect_uri` as strings in message models, requests and stored state; parse a `Uri` only transiently to inspect a part, and never store, compare or serialize the parsed `Uri`. At the token endpoint compare `redirect_uri` ordinally with the authorization request's value, treating an empty value as missing, and refuse a mismatch with `invalid_grant`.** RFC 6749 §4.1.3 requires identical values, and a parsed `Uri` no longer equals what the client sent (host case, trailing slash, user info). *Check:* Look for `Uri`-typed members holding a redirect URI, serialization via `ToString()`/`AbsoluteUri`, case-insensitive or `Uri` comparisons at the token endpoint, or an empty string treated as present. <sub>Identity ADR-1203</sub>
- **Match redirect URIs exactly: refuse an authorization request carrying more than one `redirect_uri` value, keep exact redirect_uri matching for every client, and redirect after logout only to a `post_logout_redirect_uri` that ordinally equals a registered `post_logout_redirect_uris` entry, otherwise render a confirmation page without redirecting.** Joined, prefix, normalized or case-insensitive matching enables open redirects and code leakage. *Check:* Look for redirect_uri extraction that joins or takes the first of several values, prefix/partial or case-insensitive matching, or logout code that redirects when no registered URI matches. <sub>Identity ADR-1203; Identity ADR-1380; Identity ADR-1148</sub>
- **When writing an authorization response to the redirect URI, keep the registered query and add response parameters to it (a response parameter replaces a same-named query pair), and never carry request-supplied query parameters. In the `Location` header percent-encode only characters a header cannot carry (non-ASCII, controls, space) and otherwise emit the URI as written, preserving any fragment.** RFC 6749 §3.1.2 keeps the registered query, request-supplied parameters would ride inside an accepted response, and the client must receive the response at the URI exactly as registered (RFC 3987 §3.1). *Check:* Look for response writers that drop the registered query, duplicate same-named parameters, append request parameters, or build `Location` with `Uri.AbsoluteUri`, full re-encoding or fragment stripping. <sub>Identity ADR-1203</sub>
- **Derive an authorization response's redirect target, response mode and state once per request as a single value, and show an error raised before a safe redirect target is known to the user agent instead of redirecting. Once the target is known, translate exceptions from the authorization endpoint's catch-all into a protocol error delivered to the redirect URI with `state`.** Every later response, including a signed error, must use the verified values; redirecting before verification sends the error to an unverified URI, while a known client must get its error at its redirect URI (RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1). *Check:* Look for redirect_uri, response_mode or state recomputed in several places, an error redirected before the request object or redirect URI is verified, or a generic exception handler that escapes as a server error instead of redirecting with `error` and `state`. <sub>Identity ADR-1202; Identity ADR-1428</sub>
- **Treat a private-use redirect URI scheme as valid only when it is a reverse-order domain name containing a period and no empty label.** RFC 8252 §7.1 and OAuth 2.1 §2.3.1 reject private-use schemes without a period. *Check:* Look for scheme checks that accept any non-http(s) scheme such as `myapp:`. <sub>Identity ADR-1203</sub>
- **Validate URI-valued settings the way the runtime uses them: require a scheme and no whitespace, require https for URIs the server fetches (such as `jwks_uri` and `sector_identifier_uri`), require redirect URIs to be absolute with no fragment, and require host allow-list entries to be valid hosts a parsed URI would report.** A non-https jwks_uri is never fetched, a host like `10.0.0` never matches a parsed host, and a redirect URI written as a path is not absolute. *Check:* Look for URI or host settings accepted as plain strings or checked only with `Uri.TryCreate`. <sub>Identity ADR-1140</sub>
- **Validate an issuer configured or stored as an absolute `https` URL (`http` only for a loopback host) with no user information, query, fragment or whitespace and a bounded length. Publish it byte-for-byte as the public origin clients use to reach discovery, treat it as the exact base address of its tenant's endpoints, and never append a route or path to it or hard-code a different host.** OIDC Discovery §3 and RFC 8414 §2 require this form, and conformance suites and relying parties reject discovery whose issuer differs from the discovery URL by host, scheme, port or trailing slash. *Check:* Look for issuer acceptance without these checks, issuers built from a hard-coded or request host, and code that concatenates a route or tenant path onto the issuer or publishes an `iss` different from the stored issuer. <sub>Identity ADR-1160; Identity ADR-1165; Identity docs/conformance-testing.md</sub>
- **In production code, make a frontend's configured issuer exactly the serving tenant's stored issuer (the value its discovery document publishes) or an explicit override; don't derive or normalize it separately.** The issuer a bundle trusts must equal the issuer its tokens carry under every tenant-resolution strategy. *Check:* Look for client bootstrap code that builds the issuer itself (string building, trailing-slash changes). <sub>Identity ADR-1182</sub>
- **When consuming OIDC discovery, require the returned `issuer` to equal the configured authority ordinally, require `token_endpoint` and `jwks_uri`, and validate every endpoint member present, including each `mtls_endpoint_aliases` URL, with the endpoint rule (https, or http only on loopback). Report a violation as a protocol exception.** OIDC Discovery §4.3 requires an exact issuer match, and an unchecked endpoint could send credentials to an insecure or unintended host. *Check:* Look for case-insensitive or normalized issuer comparison, unchecked required members, or endpoint and alias URLs used without scheme/host validation. <sub>Identity ADR-1285; Identity ADR-1300</sub>
- **When validating an ID token, require signature, `iss` equal to the discovered issuer, `aud` containing the client id, present `exp` and `iat`, `azp` equal to the client id when present, `typ` equal to `JWT` when present, and `nonce` and the expected `sub` equal to the caller's values by ordinal comparison, each mismatch with a distinct failure code.** OpenID Connect Core requires these checks before a client trusts the user's identity, and callers need to know which check failed. *Check:* Look for ID-token validation that skips any check, treats `exp`/`iat` as optional, ignores a present `azp`/`typ`, or compares nonce or sub case-insensitively or under a generic code. <sub>Identity ADR-1273; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md</sub>
- **When a `max_age` was requested, require `auth_time` to be a NumericDate and reject the ID token once now exceeds `auth_time + max_age` plus the allowed clock skew.** OIDC Core requires the client to enforce the `max_age` it requested. *Check:* Look for `max_age` handling that accepts a missing or non-numeric `auth_time` or omits the elapsed-time check. <sub>Identity ADR-1273; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md</sub>
- **In ID-token validation for the authorization code flow, accept a missing `at_hash`, `c_hash` or `s_hash`, but when the claim is present and the caller holds the matching value, require it to verify.** These claims are optional in the code flow (OIDC Core §3.1.3.6, §3.1.3.8), so requiring them rejects conforming providers. *Check:* Look for validation that fails on an absent hash claim, or skips verifying a present one. <sub>Identity ADR-1273</sub>
- **Take the hash function for `at_hash`, `c_hash` and `s_hash` from the signing algorithm's defined token-hash function, never from the `alg` name's suffix or only from `HashAlgorithmName`.** The suffix names the wrong digest for Ed25519 and Ed448; Ed448 uses SHAKE256 with 114 bytes, which `HashAlgorithmName` cannot name, and polymorphic EdDSA picks its hash by the key's curve. *Check:* Look for code that parses a `256`/`384`/`512` suffix, switches on alg strings, or maps `HashAlgorithmName` directly to compute token hashes. <sub>Identity ADR-1273; Identity ADR-1392</sub>
- **Validate a back-channel logout token under Back-Channel Logout 1.0 §2.6: signature, `iss`, `aud` and `iat` as for other provider JWTs; `typ` `logout+jwt` when present; at least one of `sub` and `sid`, each non-empty when present; `sid` present when the client registered `backchannel_logout_session_required`; `events` an object whose `http://schemas.openid.net/event/backchannel-logout` member is an object; no `nonce`; and a non-empty string `jti`.** A logout token has different required claims and `typ` from an ID token, and these checks stop one being presented as the other. *Check:* Look for logout-token validation missing the `typ`, `events`, nonce-absent or sid/sub checks, or accepting empty `sub`/`sid`. <sub>Identity ADR-1274; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md</sub>
- **A receiver of retried deliveries (an OIDC back-channel logout endpoint, a webhook) only looks a dedupe key such as `jti` up during validation and records it only after handling has succeeded and every other check passed; when handling fails it answers so the sender retries (400 for back-channel logout) without recording the key.** The sender retries a failed delivery with the same token; recording first turns the retry into a refused replay and the sessions are never ended (Back-Channel Logout §2.8). *Check:* Look for a replay-store add inside a validate method, recording before the sessions are ended, recording on an error path, or 200 when ending sessions failed. <sub>Identity ADR-1274; Identity ADR-1280; Identity ADR-1293; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md</sub>
- **A back-channel logout receiver finds sessions through `sid`/`sub` indexes, not by scanning the store, and ends a candidate only when it matches the token's issuer, its `sid` when present, and the receiving client. Require `sid` by default (matching a registered `backchannel_logout_session_required=true`) and accept `sub`-only tokens only when an explicit option allows it. Answer 200 with `Cache-Control: no-store` on success and 400 when the request or token is invalid, the provider's keys can't be read or a session can't be ended.** Scanning doesn't scale, unchecked matches let one token end another issuer's or client's sessions, and `sub`-only acceptance lets one provider session end all of a user's sessions. *Check:* Look for store enumeration, sessions ended without issuer, sid and client checks, a session-required option defaulting to false, or wrong status codes or missing no-store. <sub>Identity ADR-1293; Identity ADR-1442</sub>
- **Validate a token's claims in a fixed order: algorithm policy, then decrypt, signature, issuer, audience, lifetime, then the encryption requirement, header-replicated `iss` and `typ`, then claim checks. When a JWE header replicates `iss` (RFC 7519 §5.3), require a string equal to the expected issuer or fail with `invalid_issuer`.** No check may run before the algorithm policy, and a replicated header claim that mismatches must not be ignored. *Check:* Look for checks moved before the algorithm policy, or JWE handling that ignores or accepts a non-string or mismatched header `iss`. <sub>Identity ADR-1280</sub>
- **Validate JWTs only in the compact serializations, refuse the JWS/JWE JSON serializations, and when encoding a signed-and-encrypted token emit a JWE with `cty` `JWT` enclosing the JWS (RFC 7519 §5.2).** RFC 7519 represents a JWT only compactly; JSON serializations carry several signatures or recipients, and the validator accepts an encrypted token only when marked as a nested JWT. *Check:* Look for JWT validation that parses JSON-serialized input, or an encoder that encrypts a signed JWT without `cty: JWT`. <sub>Identity ADR-1154</sub>
- **In production code, split a compact JWS or JWE with `MemoryExtensions.Split` into a `stackalloc Range[segmentCount + 1]` and reject any count but `segmentCount`, and take the JWS signing input as a slice of the original token text, never `string.Split` or a re-concatenated string.** The spare slot makes extra segments exceed the limit instead of folding into the last range, and re-concatenation allocates and can differ from the signed bytes. *Check:* Look for `string.Split('.')` on tokens, a Range buffer sized exactly to the segment count, or `header + "." + payload` for verification. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Always validate a request object's `aud` against the configured expected audience or, when none is configured, the authorization server's issuer, and refuse a request object without `aud` with `invalid_request_object`. Refuse one lacking response_type, scope, redirect_uri or client_id, or whose outer response_type, redirect_uri or client_id (when sent) differs from the object's; ignore the outer scope.** An unchecked `aud` lets a request object for another server be replayed (RFC 9101, FAPI), and a code must never go to one URI while being redeemable only with another; the object's scope supersedes the outer one (OIDC Core §6.1). *Check:* Look for JAR loading that skips `aud` when unconfigured, accepts a missing `aud`, doesn't enforce required members, or doesn't compare sent outer values. <sub>Identity ADR-1187; Identity ADR-1202</sub>
- **Don't report a request object loader for not requiring the `typ` header `oauth-authz-req+jwt` when it validates `iss` against the client, `aud` against the issuer, and the client's signature.** Requiring the explicit `typ` would refuse every OIDC Core client and the conformance suite; the audience and issuer checks already prevent confusion. *Check:* Before raising a missing-`typ` finding on request objects, confirm the iss, aud and signature checks exist. <sub>Identity ADR-1187</sub>
- **Set an access token's `aud` to the identifiers of the enabled resource servers owning its effective scopes, not the client id; fall back to the client id only for a scopeless token so no token lacks an audience. Always set an ID token's `aud` to the client id.** An audience equal to the client id confuses requester with recipient, so a resource server couldn't tell tokens minted for it; OIDC requires the ID token's audience to be the client. *Check:* Look for access-token minting that sets `aud` to the client id while scopes are present or can emit no `aud`, or ID-token creation deriving `aud` from resources or scopes. <sub>Identity ADR-1026</sub>
- **Emit `aud` as a string for one audience and an array for several, and validate it by checking that it contains the expected identifier, accepting the array form.** RFC 7519 allows an array, and a resource server validates by finding its own identifier. *Check:* Look for audience validation comparing `aud` as one string, or emission that always uses one form. <sub>Identity ADR-1026</sub>
- **Apply the audience rule consistently across token formats: when the verifier names no valid audiences, refuse a token that carries `aud`; when it names some, require the token's `aud` to contain one of them; a token without `aud` is valid only for a verifier that names none.** This follows RFC 8392 §3.1.3 and RFC 7519 §4.1.3; some tokens such as status lists legitimately carry no `aud`. *Check:* Look for audience checks skipped when the configured list is empty, or that always require `aud`. <sub>Identity ADR-1410</sub>
- **Treat RFC 8707 `resource` values only as a narrowing of the scope-derived audience: match them ordinally against known resource identifiers, never let them add access the client holds no scope for, refuse unknown, unauthorized or non-matching values with `invalid_target`, and at code redemption refuse a `resource` the authorization request didn't authorize. Don't add discovery metadata advertising resource-indicator support.** Narrowing gives least privilege and FAPI audience binding; a token request may only narrow the authorization. Neither RFC 8707 nor RFC 8414 defines such metadata. *Check:* Look for code that adds audiences or scopes from `resource`, ignores invalid values, uses another error, compares case-insensitively or by URI syntax, skips the subset check at redemption, or advertises resource-indicator metadata. <sub>Identity ADR-1026</sub>
- **Enforce audience resolution and `resource` narrowing at one shared token-minting path that every grant type goes through.** A single choke point gives every grant the same narrowing and enforcement. *Check:* Look for a new grant or token path that mints an access token outside the shared minting path or duplicates its audience logic. <sub>Identity ADR-1026</sub>
- **Compare OAuth scope tokens in protocol requests case-sensitively and ordinally, and reject a requested scope outside the client's allowed set with `invalid_scope`.** RFC 6749 defines scope tokens as case-sensitive, and validators must refuse scopes the client may not request. *Check:* Look for case-insensitive comparers or ToLower/ToUpper on requested scopes, or out-of-set scopes dropped silently or answered with another error. *Note:* Management APIs that look scopes up in a store enforcing case-insensitive uniqueness match with OrdinalIgnoreCase (see the management-scope rule); check the store's normalization before reporting. <sub>Identity ADR-1026</sub>
- **When a management route matches a scope value from the request against stored scopes in a store that enforces case-insensitive uniqueness, compare with `StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase` like its sibling lookups, and write the stored scope's own value and flags, not the route's spelling. Don't ask for ordinal comparison there.** Ordinal matching against a case-insensitive store plans a value the store then refuses, and the stored entity is authoritative. *Check:* Before reporting OrdinalIgnoreCase on scope values, check how the store normalizes them and how sibling lookups compare; flag writes that persist the route value. <sub>Identity ADR-1483; Identity outcomes of #592</sub>
- **Issue a refresh token only when the client requested `offline_access` and `refresh_token` is a supported grant type. An OIDC client must not add `offline_access` on its own: request `openid` plus the configured scopes, each once.** Issuance depends on both conditions, and `offline_access` asks for a grant that outlives the login session; some OPs then detach it so back-channel logout never reaches the client. *Check:* Look for refresh-token issuance missing either check, or client code that appends `offline_access` automatically or sends duplicate scopes. <sub>Identity ADR-1026; Identity ADR-1291</sub>
- **Present a rotating refresh token to the provider at most once cluster-wide: guard each refresh with a single-flight lease keyed by a fingerprint (e.g. SHA-256) of the refresh token itself, re-read the session under the lease, and have a loser wait with backoff and retry only for a changed token or a released lease. Never present a token whose lease another holder has, even after a wait timeout (fail, e.g. 503).** Presenting a rotated token twice is reuse that revokes the whole family (RFC 9700 §4.14.2); record versions change on unrelated writes and would admit a second refresher. *Check:* Look for concurrent refresh without a lease, leases keyed by record version or session id, no re-read under the lock, or timeout paths that call the token endpoint with the original token. <sub>Identity ADR-1291</sub>
- **Once a refresh-token request has started, run the token request and the write-back of the new tokens with `CancellationToken.None`, and when the write-back loses an optimistic-concurrency race, merge onto the newer version and retry instead of dropping it.** An abort after the provider rotated the token, or a dropped write, loses the only copy of the rotated token. *Check:* Check that refresh request and persistence don't pass the caller's token, and that version conflicts on write-back retry with a merge. <sub>Identity ADR-1291</sub>
- **Don't rotate, by default, the refresh token of a confidential client or one bound to a DPoP key or certificate; rotate only on explicit opt-in, and make a FAPI 2.0 profile reset rather than inherit an 'always rotate' default.** FAPI 2.0 §5.3.2.1 forbids rotation for sender-constrained confidential clients; it adds no security there and a lost rotation response loses the session. *Check:* Look at default rotation policy and profile defaults for rotating bound or confidential clients' tokens. <sub>Identity ADR-1216</sub>
- **Answer a refresh-token retry only while it can still issue a refresh token: `offline_access` is in the effective scopes, the grant names a lineage, and the lineage still has an active grant; otherwise return `invalid_grant` with no replay audit event and no family revocation.** A retry recovers a lost rotation; once the family can't issue refresh tokens there is nothing to recover and it isn't a compromise signal. *Check:* Check that the retry path tests scope, lineage and active grant, and that its refusal branch doesn't audit a replay or revoke the family. <sub>Identity ADR-1217</sub>
- **Under a sliding refresh-token policy, set a token's expiry to the sliding lifetime from issue or last use, capped at the family's fixed horizon; under an absolute policy, set every token's expiry to the horizon. Every token response carrying a refresh token, from any grant or delivery, includes `refresh_token_expires_in` as the whole seconds left until the family horizon, and introspection reports a refresh token inactive once its family is past the horizon.** Sliding promises extension only up to an absolute maximum; clients bound sessions by a horizon that never moves later; introspection must agree with the refresh grant. *Check:* Flag uncapped sliding expiry, absolute expiry computed per token, responses omitting `refresh_token_expires_in` or computing it from the token's own expiry, and introspection that ignores the family horizon. <sub>Identity ADR-1297</sub>
- **In an OAuth client, treat a token response without `expires_in` as already expiring, read `refresh_token_expires_in` leniently (ignore a value that isn't a positive whole number), and use it only to shorten the session's and cookie's lifetime, never to extend it.** A missing lifetime can't be trusted, the member is advisory and non-standard, and the refresh horizon bounds how long the session can obtain tokens. *Check:* Look for assumed default lifetimes, strict parsing that fails the response, or session expiry set from the value without taking the minimum with the existing expiry. <sub>Identity ADR-1291; Identity ADR-1297; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md</sub>
- **Make the token revocation endpoint answer 200 to every authenticated request whether the token was revoked, unknown or not revocable, and 400 `invalid_request` only when `token` is missing. Treat revocation of a self-contained JWT access token as an accepted no-op; don't add a per-token denylist or a revocation lookup to access-token validation.** RFC 7009 requires this leniency and other answers make the endpoint an oracle; a denylist adds per-token state and a lookup per resource call, which stateless JWTs exist to avoid. *Check:* Look for non-200 results or state-dependent responses for unknown, expired, revoked or unsupported tokens, and new access-token denylist tables, caches or lookups. <sub>Identity ADR-1028</sub>
- **Make the introspection endpoint answer `400 invalid_request` only when `token` is missing and 200 otherwise; for an inactive token (invalid, expired, revoked, foreign, wrong caller) return exactly `{"active": false}`. A JWT introspection response (RFC 9701) uses `typ` `token-introspection+jwt`, carries only `iss`, `aud` (the resource server) and `iat` at top level with the result under `token_introspection`, and never a top-level `sub` or `exp`.** RFC 7662 says inactive tokens reveal nothing; without top-level `sub`/`exp` the JWT response can't be mistaken for an access token. *Check:* Flag extra members or errors next to `active: false`, 4xx/5xx for bad tokens, another `typ`, flattened result claims, or a top-level `sub`/`exp`. <sub>Identity ADR-1168</sub>
- **Client authentication handlers form a strategy collection: each method has its own handler and descriptor; a handler claims a request only when the client's registered `token_endpoint_auth_method` equals its method (a JWT assertion handler also requires `client_assertion_type` exactly `urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer`, read only from a form POST body) and otherwise returns undefined so a sibling can handle it; once it claims the request, a missing or non-matching credential is a conclusive `invalid_client`.** Each method is advertised and registered separately; a certificate presented only for token binding must not count as authentication; once owned there is no fallback. *Check:* Look for one handler serving several methods, handlers triggered by the mere presence of a certificate or credential, assertions read from query or headers, or fall-through after claiming. <sub>Identity ADR-1102; Identity ADR-1173</sub>
- **When authenticating a client from a JWT assertion, require `iss` and `sub` both present and equal, locate the client by `sub`, and don't require a separate `client_id` parameter. By default accept an `aud` that is the issuer, the endpoint's URL under the base address, or the endpoint's URL under the mTLS alias; restrict it to the issuer only when a security profile such as FAPI requires.** OIDC Core §9 pins iss == sub == client_id and allows the endpoint URL as audience; FAPI private_key_jwt clients send only the assertion and FAPI narrows `aud` to the issuer. *Check:* Look for a missing iss/sub equality, lookup by `iss` alone, rejection for a missing `client_id` form parameter, default validation rejecting the endpoint URL, or audiences outside the tenant's published URLs. <sub>Identity ADR-1102; Identity ADR-1365</sub>
- **Compare a client assertion's `aud` or a DPoP proof's `htu` with the endpoint URL the tenant publishes, built the same way discovery builds it: authority from the tenant's issuer base address or its mTLS alias (RFC 8705 §5), only the routed path from the request. Compare `htu` with exactly one URL, the alias one when the request arrived on the alias host and port and otherwise the base one; never accept a match against any of several.** A URL from the request's Host would accept proofs minted for another server, and RFC 9449 §4.3 binds a proof to the URL actually called. *Check:* Look for comparisons against URLs built from the request scheme and host, built differently from discovery, or checked against a candidate set. <sub>Identity ADR-1365</sub>
- **When creating a `private_key_jwt` client assertion (RFC 7523), set `iss` and `sub` to the client id, `aud` to the provider's issuer as a single string (not the token endpoint URL), `jti` to 16 random bytes in base64url, `iat` and `nbf` to now and `exp` 60 seconds later.** RFC 7523bis and FAPI 2.0 require the issuer as audience, and a short fixed lifetime with a random `jti` limits replay. *Check:* Look for `aud` set to the token endpoint or an array, a low-entropy or missing `jti`, or a configurable or long lifetime. <sub>Identity ADR-1285</sub>

- **Make logout behave as discovery advertises: send no back-channel logout token while `backchannel_logout_supported` is false, omit `sid` while `backchannel_logout_session_supported` is false, and append front-channel `iss`/`sid` query parameters only while `frontchannel_logout_session_supported` is enabled.** The OP must not behave differently from what its discovery document advertises. *Check:* Look for notifiers or front-channel URI builders that send tokens or add sid/iss without checking the setting. <sub>Identity ADR-1380; Identity ADR-1088</sub>

- **An end-session endpoint asks the end user to confirm whenever an OP login exists and the request carries no valid `id_token_hint` whose `sid` ordinally equals the login's `sid`, and never signs the user out unprompted in that case.** RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 §2 requires the prompt and it closes logout CSRF. *Check:* Look for a path that ends the session without a matching-sid hint or confirmation, or non-ordinal sid comparison. <sub>Identity ADR-1380</sub>

- **When validating a subject outside a protocol request, pass a null request rather than a fabricated one; the validator then skips only the request-dependent checks (`max_age`, `idp:` acr_values, essential acr) and runs all others.** A fabricated request misrepresents the context. *Check:* Look for placeholder requests built for subject validation, or validators skipping more than the request-dependent checks on null. <sub>Identity ADR-1225</sub>

- **Don't report a missing no-store header on a response written before the endpoint filter runs, such as a 400 for a body that fails to bind or a 401/403 from an outer filter.** Those responses carry no secret. *Check:* Confirm the response is produced ahead of the filter and carries no secret before reporting. <sub>Identity ADR-1050</sub>

- **In server-driven content negotiation for OAuth/OIDC responses, select an alternate formatter only for an explicit `type/subtype` in Accept; a wildcard-only or missing Accept yields the JSON wire default.** curl and programmatic callers send `*/*` and expect JSON; only browsers listing `text/html` should get HTML. *Check:* Look for negotiation letting `*/*` or `type/*` select HTML or another non-JSON formatter. <sub>Identity ADR-1114</sub>

- **Return an `x-fapi-interaction-id` header from every OpenID protocol endpoint, set in one filter on the protocol endpoint group before the next delegate runs and outside the rate-limit and environment filters: echo the request value only when it is a canonical hyphenated UUID, with its exact text and case, else generate a new UUID.** FAPI 1.0 Part 1 §6.2.1-11 requires it on every response including refusals, and echoing arbitrary strings carries untrusted input into logs. *Check:* Look for unvalidated echoes, case changes, endpoints outside the filtered group, headers set after `next`, or the filter registered inside the refusing filters. <sub>Identity ADR-1498</sub>
- **Retry an outbound HTTP request only when it is safe to send twice: a bodiless GET or HEAD, on `HttpRequestException`, the attempt timeout's `TimeoutRejectedException`, 408, 429 or 5xx, with exponential jittered backoff and `Retry-After` never extending the delay past the total timeout; never resend a request with content, a non-idempotent method, or a single-use proof.** OAuth endpoints honor no idempotency key, so codes and refresh tokens must never be sent twice; jitter avoids synchronized retries. *Check:* Look for retries applied to every request, POST/PUT/PATCH or content-bearing requests, DPoP requests, constant delays, other 4xx, or waiting on Retry-After. *Note:* For calls to caller-supplied URLs the stricter rule applies: no retry on connection or name-resolution errors and `Retry-After` ignored. <sub>Identity ADR-1336; Identity docs/metrics.md</sub>

- **A server-written page hosting a mountable frontend bundle writes `<base href="{mount path}/">` first in `<head>` and uses page-relative form actions and asset URLs.** The bundle resolves paths against `document.baseURI`, so one build mounts anywhere. *Check:* Look for pages without a leading base element or with absolute or root-level actions or assets. <sub>Identity ADR-1193</sub>
- **Never treat an unsupported `ui_locales` preference as an error; select a locale by RFC 4647 §3.4 lookup per preference, case-insensitively, with the tenant's supported-locales ceiling applied to the fallback default too; and carry the preference across an authorization or end-session flow's interactive pages on the redirect URL's `ui_locales` query and a hidden form field, not by store lookups or a cookie.** OIDC Core §3.1.2.1 says it SHOULD NOT error; the ceiling keeps rendering consistent with discovery; per-request store reads are a cost any caller can impose and cookies add a second source of truth. *Check:* Look for validation rejecting ui_locales, exact or case-sensitive matching, fallbacks skipping the ceiling, pages loading stored state or cookies for locale, or redirects dropping the value. <sub>Identity ADR-1402</sub>
- **Don't ask account-management pages outside an authorization or end-session flow to carry `ui_locales`.** They render from Accept-Language and tenant settings by decision. *Check:* Check whether the page belongs to such a flow before reporting. <sub>Identity outcomes of #548</sub>
- **Resolve SD-JWT disclosures per RFC 9901 §7.1 and refuse every ambiguity with its own failure code (repeated digests, shared disclosures, object/array kind mismatch, collisions, unreferenced disclosures, misplaced reserved names, malformed `_sd`/`...`), dropping unmatched digests only as decoys. Compute disclosure digests over the base64url text as received and `sd_hash` over the presentation exactly as received through the last `~`. In issuance, refuse to make a profile's required claims disclosable.** Ambiguity lets a holder change what a verifier reads, re-encoding changes bytes, and verifiers check required claims on the signed payload. *Check:* Check each refusal case and code, digests over re-encoded JSON, and issuer validation allowing required claims to be disclosable. <sub>Identity ADR-1405; Identity outcomes of #552</sub>
- **Validate a KB-JWT as `kb+jwt` with the holder key, the required algorithms and the verifier's audience, refusing it as not fresh when `iat` is missing, later than now plus skew, or older than the maximum age plus skew.** Freshness and audience binding stop replay of captured presentations. *Check:* Check typ, audience, iat presence and both freshness bounds. <sub>Identity ADR-1405</sub>
- **CBOR/COSE writers produce RFC 8949 §4.2.1 core deterministic encoding (definite lengths, shortest integers, map keys sorted bytewise by encoded label, not `CborConformanceMode.Canonical`) and an empty protected header as a zero-length byte string; readers accept that or an encoded empty map, authenticate protected bytes as received, and refuse an untagged message unless the caller names the type.** Canonical mode sorts length-first, RFC 9052 requires the empty bstr and signs protected bytes as received, and untagged input can't be identified safely. *Check:* Look for Canonical mode, indefinite lengths, insertion-order maps, empty-map protected headers written, readers re-encoding headers, or decoders guessing untagged structures. <sub>Identity ADR-1409</sub>
- **Don't report that a COSE reader fails to enforce deterministic map order on received input.** RFC 9052 §9 requires deterministic encoding only for structures the library builds. *Check:* Confirm the code parses received data before raising a canonicalization finding. <sub>Identity ADR-1409</sub>
- **Map a binary COSE `kid` to a text key identifier through one shared mapping: UTF-8 when valid text not starting with `h'`, otherwise RFC 8949 §8 `h'...'` notation; don't refuse binary kids or base64url-encode every kid.** RFC 8747's example kid is binary and text kids must stay readable, consistently everywhere. *Check:* Look for ad hoc base64url, hex or unvalidated UTF-8 kid conversions. <sub>Identity ADR-1409</sub>
- **Match X.500 distinguished names with RFC 4517 `distinguishedNameMatch` (same RDN count and order, equal OIDs, values prepared per RFC 4518), never by DER bytes or `X500DistinguishedName.Name` strings; read a forwarded client-certificate header holding a comma-separated chain with the leaf first and pass the rest on as intermediates.** CAs differ in string types and case that the RFC treats as equal, and chain building needs the forwarded intermediates. *Check:* Look for `RawData` or Name/Subject string equality, ad-hoc DN parsing, or forwarded-certificate parsing that decodes the whole value, picks the wrong leaf or drops intermediates. <sub>Identity ADR-1173; Identity docs/hosting-analysis.md</sub>
- **Build OCSP requests to the RFC 5019 lightweight profile (one CertID with SHA-1 hashes, no requestor name, signature or nonce; GET when the URL is at most 255 characters, else POST `application/ocsp-request`), fall through to CRL sources when OCSP fails or answers `unknown`, and in an indirect CRL let `certificateIssuer` set the issuer of its and following entries, match on serial and issuer, and don't count `removeFromCRL` as revoked.** Pre-produced responses can't echo nonces and nonces defeat caching; PKIs keep working when the responder is down; indirect CRLs list several CAs. *Check:* Look for nonce extensions or signatures, fixed methods, terminal results on OCSP failure, serial-only matching, per-entry issuer reset, or removeFromCRL counted. <sub>Identity ADR-1259</sub>
- **Make a backend-for-frontend a confidential OAuth client using `private_key_jwt` or mTLS, authorization code with PKCE S256, PAR when advertised, RFC 9207 `iss` checks and DPoP when supported; don't implement implicit, hybrid or password flows or return tokens to browser script. Rely only on standard OP metadata and client registration, with no provider-specific branches or provider features added just for the BFF.** This is current best practice; tokens in script reach are unsafe; the BFF must run against any compliant provider. *Check:* Look for client secrets instead of assertions, missing or plain PKCE, ignored PAR/DPoP metadata, `token`/`id_token` response types, password grants, endpoints returning tokens to the SPA, hard-coded paths, provider-specific branches, or BFF-only OP settings. <sub>Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity ADR-1294</sub>
- **A BFF answers a guarded API call or user-info request without a live session with 401 and the session_required problem type, never a redirect or 403; its user-info endpoint only reads the session and never slides its idle expiry; and it pushes no session-ended events over server-sent events, WebSockets or new pub/sub.** The 401 is the single signal frontends rely on across replicas, polls must not keep sessions alive, and push streams starve per-origin connections and need cross-replica plumbing. *Check:* Look for redirects or 403 on guarded endpoints, session or cookie renewal on the user-info path, or new text/event-stream or WebSocket endpoints for session end. <sub>Identity ADR-1434</sub>
- **A BFF-served frontend that learns its session ended (logout, 401 session_required, expiry, failed refresh) broadcasts it to other tabs via BroadcastChannel and shows a sign-in screen whose button starts login, never navigating to the login endpoint on its own; its session probes send the anti-forgery header and recheck on visibilitychange; and it signs out by POSTing the BFF's logout form with `sid` and a return URL.** Automatic navigation races logouts and loops on failing logins, BroadcastChannel alone misses server-side endings, hidden tabs' timers are throttled, and logout is a form post bound to the session. *Check:* Look for `window.location` set to login from session handlers, handlers not notifying other tabs or relying only on BroadcastChannel, probes without the anti-forgery header or visibility recheck, or GET logout links. *Note:* An earlier decision allowed navigating to login directly; the newer decision (ADR-1438) requires the sign-in screen. <sub>Identity ADR-1438; Identity ADR-1434</sub>
- **A request to a hub must not write a cookie to the upgraded response; it slides the session and obtains tokens through the connection's in-memory session handle.** The upgraded response has already started and the connection has no `HttpContext` after opening. *Check:* Look for session refresh or Set-Cookie writes on hub or WebSocket code paths. <sub>Identity ADR-1435</sub>
- **Don't detect a cross-site or redirected top-level navigation from `Sec-Fetch-Site`; key it on the method, `Sec-Fetch-Mode` absent or `navigate`, and the Strict session cookie being absent, and bound any automatic reload with a short-lived marker such as a `__Host-` Secure HttpOnly cookie with Max-Age about 60 seconds.** Browsers label the same navigation differently, and an unbounded reload loops forever. *Check:* Flag logic branching on Sec-Fetch-Site and reload responses without a marker or limit. <sub>Identity ADR-1292</sub>
- **In a multi-client deployment, require each OAuth client's callback URI to be unique across clients and make the client selectable from the URLs the OP is told (callback, back-channel logout, JWKS), with a back-channel logout ending only the receiving client's sessions.** The OP must tell clients apart, and one client's logout must not end another's sessions. *Check:* Look for configuration validation missing duplicate-callback checks, selection only via routing such as `RequireHost`, or logout lookups without a client filter. <sub>Identity ADR-1442</sub>
- **Forward HTTP requests through YARP's `IHttpForwarder` rather than a hand-written HttpClient proxy.** It handles streaming, hop-by-hop headers and protocol edge cases correctly. *Check:* Look for proxy code copying requests and responses by hand. <sub>Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md</sub>
- **A cross-replica change announcement carries only an identifier of what changed; receivers re-read or evict.** It is a hint; the source of truth stays in storage and materialized state may not be serializable. *Check:* Look for broadcasts serializing entity state, settings or secrets. <sub>Identity ADR-1205</sub>
- **A structured record emitted for others (audit record, webhook or event payload) is documented and updated in the same change, carries a schema version whose minor part is bumped when a field is added, omits absent members and empty arrays instead of writing null, uses the same field names in logs, spans and metrics, and for audit events uses UUIDv7 ids and UTC RFC 3339 times with a `Z` suffix.** It is a contract consumers rely on, and UUIDv7 ids sort and paginate by time. *Check:* Look for payload changes without doc or version updates, `WriteNull` or empty arrays, inconsistent names, `Guid.NewGuid()` event ids, or local/offset times. <sub>Identity docs/audit-records.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md</sub>
- **In production code, give a JSON-deserialized DTO a `[JsonExtensionData] public Dictionary<string, JsonElement>? ExtensionData { get; set; }` member.** Unrecognized wire members then round-trip instead of being dropped. *Check:* Look for deserialized DTOs without a JsonExtensionData member. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Reject a request to remove a resource's last owner with 409 Conflict.** A resource keeps at least one owner. *Check:* Check owner-revocation endpoints for a last-owner guard. <sub>Identity ADR-1417</sub>
- **When a script, command or code reads a paged API (GraphQL `first:` connections, REST `per_page`, `gh api`/`glab` list calls) and relies on the full result, page through it (for example `gh api --paginate --slurp`) or check `pageInfo.hasNextPage` and report a partial result; read a list's newest item with `last:`, and when replacing a CLI list command with its REST form, pass the sort and order the caller relies on (e.g. `sort=updated&order=desc`). A deliberate single-page read carries an adjacent comment stating the cap and why it suffices.** Items past the cap are otherwise silently dropped, and search defaults to best-match order. *Check:* Look for `first: N` without pageInfo, `per_page` without pagination or a justifying comment, last items taken from a `first:` window, or search calls without sort parameters. <sub>project-template outcomes of #124; project-template outcomes of #146; project-template outcomes of #148; project-template outcomes of #244</sub>
- **Don't ask for a page loop or paging test on a single-page list call whose comment states the cap and why the filtered result stays below it, and don't report a partial-update call missing a body field when the API reference marks the field optional and a guard ensures the resource is already in the required state.** The maintainer declined both findings: a documented cap adds nothing to loop over, and optional fields need not be sent. *Check:* Read the comment above the call, or the endpoint's documented body fields and the preceding guard, before reporting. <sub>project-template outcomes of #244; project-template outcomes of #140</sub>
- **Probes for an HTTPS-only ASP.NET Core pod use `scheme: HTTPS` and send a `Host` header that `AllowedHosts` accepts; startup and liveness probes call the liveness endpoint and only readiness calls the readiness endpoint.** The kubelet sends the pod IP as Host, which AllowedHosts rejects, and liveness must not check dependencies. *Check:* Inspect probe scheme, a non-wildcard httpHeaders Host entry, and each probe's health path. <sub>Identity ADR-1458</sub>
- **In production code, to pre-fill an `x-www-form-urlencoded` field in an API-reference renderer, mark it required and set its schema `Default` in a document transformer rather than a named example, and place credentials where the client's registered authentication method expects them.** Renderers omit optional properties and ignore examples, and misplaced credentials fail authentication. *Check:* Look for transformers pre-filling via `example`, or credential locations not matching the auth method (client_secret_basic needs the Authorization header). *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
